name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Clay Fuller running for reelection
Harris's large fundraising but heavy outside opposition spending
model.rationale: The R+19 district and an incumbent Republican make this a Safe R race; markets price a Republican win around 94%. Harris's $8.1 million in fundraising is notable but came with heavy outside opposition and little cash on hand, and no polls or expert ratings suggest a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Harris converting his fundraising advantage into a single-digit race would warrant a move toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Northwest Georgia's 14th District is deeply Republican territory, with a partisan lean of R+19. Incumbent Clay Fuller is running for reelection after easily securing renomination, and outside groups have spent heavily to support him while attacking his challenger. Shawn Harris has raised an unusually large sum for a Democrat in this district, but outside opposition spending against him has also been substantial and he ends with little cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings are available for the general election. Prediction markets give Fuller roughly a 94% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican margin in the mid-to-high teens, consistent with the district's lean adjusted slightly for the incumbent's position. Harris's fundraising is the main reason not to write the race off entirely, but nothing in the evidence suggests a genuine upset threat.
